// File retains logical paths and exact source bytes. Dependencies are not
// checkable inputs. OSG deliberately supplies its libraries as ordinary files.
type File struct { Filename, Raw string }
type Issue struct {
 Filename, Key, Severity, Message string
 Row, Column, EndRow, EndColumn int32
}
// ParseRuns/ParseObjects count pending invalidations submitted after Update.
// Untouched inert objects are excluded even if the core never clears their dirty flag.
type Stats struct {
 Updates, Noops, IndexedObjects, ReaderVisits, DirtiedObjects, ParseRuns, ParseObjects int32
}

// Generated core globals assume sequential execution, including across Checkers.
var libraryMu sync.Mutex
var libraryWords = regexp.MustCompile(`(/[A-Z0-9_]{1,10}/)?[A-Z0-9_]{1,40}`)

// Checker owns a persistent registry. A global libraryMu serialises all Checkers,
// including reads: one checking thread per process.
// Failures panic with a cause: the host must
// refuse that check. Failed Prime/Update requires re-prime; a failed Check can
// be retried after the host restores an overlay with Update.
type Checker struct {
 registry @Registry@
 readers map[string]map[@Object@]bool
 words map[@Object@][]string
 pending map[@Object@]bool
 stats Stats
}

// Prime replaces the baseline, including files, dependencies and config.
func (c *Checker) Prime(files, deps []File, config string) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 *c = Checker{readers: map[string]map[@Object@]bool{}, words: map[@Object@][]string{}, pending: map[@Object@]bool{}}
 h := @newRun@()
 for _, f := range files { h.@addFile@(str(f.Filename), str(f.Raw)) }
 for _, f := range deps { h.@addDependency@(str(f.Filename), str(f.Raw)) }
 c.registry = h.@parse@(str(config))
 // Iterate owners once. Looking up every filename here would scan the
 // entire registry twice per input and make priming quadratic.
 objects := c.registry.@getObjects@()
 defer objects.@close@()
 for {
  next := objects.@next@()
  if next.@done@ { break }
  c.index(next.@value@)
 }
}

func (c *Checker) require() {
 if c.registry == nil { panic("prime must succeed before check/update") }
}

func (c *Checker) index(obj @Object@) {
 c.stats.IndexedObjects++
 seen := map[string]bool{}
 files := obj.@getFiles@()
 for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(files); i++ {
  file := any(libraryAt(files, i)).(@File@)
  for _, word := range libraryWords.FindAllString(strings.ToUpper(file.@getRaw@().String()), -1) { seen[word] = true }
 }
 c.words[obj] = make([]string, 0, len(seen))
 for word := range seen {
  if c.readers[word] == nil { c.readers[word] = map[@Object@]bool{} }
  c.readers[word][obj] = true
  c.words[obj] = append(c.words[obj], word)
 }
}
func (c *Checker) unindex(obj @Object@) {
 for _, word := range c.words[obj] {
  delete(c.readers[word], obj)
  if len(c.readers[word]) == 0 { delete(c.readers, word) }
 }
 delete(c.words, obj)
}

// Update batches edits without parsing. nil removes a file; &"" installs an
// empty file. The host implements overlay+restore by deferring Update(original).
// Only direct lexical readers are invalidated, including comments/strings.
// Following readers transitively discards unrelated parsed trees and definitions.
func (c *Checker) Update(filename string, raw *string) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 c.require()
 c.stats.Updates++
 before := c.registry.@getFileByName@(str(filename))
 if raw == nil && before == nil || raw != nil && before != nil && before.@getRaw@().String() == *raw { c.stats.Noops++; return }
 var old @Object@
 if before != nil { old = c.registry.@findObjectForFile@(before) }
 if old != nil { c.unindex(old); delete(c.pending, old) }
 file := before
 var obj @Object@
 if raw == nil {
  c.registry.@removeFile@(before)
  if old != nil && libraryLength(old.@getFiles@()) > 0 { obj = old }
 } else {
  file = @newFile@(str(filename), str(*raw))
  if before == nil { c.registry.@addFile@(file) } else { c.registry.@updateFile@(file) }
  obj = c.registry.@findObjectForFile@(file)
 }
 dirty := map[@Object@]bool{}
 if obj != nil { c.index(obj); dirty[obj] = true }
 name := strings.ToUpper(file.@getObjectName@().String())
 for reader := range c.readers[name] {
  c.stats.ReaderVisits++
  if dirty[reader] { continue }
  dirty[reader] = true
  reader.@setDirty@()
 }
 for object := range dirty { c.pending[object] = true }
 c.stats.DirtiedObjects += int32(len(dirty))
}

// Full-core arrays can be live views; small emitted packages use plain Items.
func libraryLength[T any](values *array[T]) int32 {
 if live, ok := any(values).(interface{ liveLength() int32 }); ok { return live.liveLength() }
 return int32(len(values.Items))
}
func libraryAt[T any](values *array[T], at int32) T {
 value := values.get(at)
 if !value.Has { panic("unexpected hole in core result array") }
 return value.Value
}

func libraryCoordinate(value any) int32 {
 var n float64
 switch v := value.(type) {
 case float64: n = v
 case int64: n = float64(v)
 case int32: n = float64(v)
 case optional[float64]: if !v.Has { panic("issue coordinate is undefined") }; n = v.Value
 case optional[int64]: if !v.Has { panic("issue coordinate is undefined") }; n = float64(v.Value)
 case optional[int32]: if !v.Has { panic("issue coordinate is undefined") }; n = float64(v.Value)
 default: panic(fmt.Sprintf("unsupported issue coordinate %T", value))
 }
 if math.IsNaN(n) || math.IsInf(n, 0) || math.Trunc(n) != n || n < math.MinInt32 || n > math.MaxInt32 { panic("issue coordinate is not a finite int32") }
 return int32(n)
}

// Check parses dirty objects lazily and runs rules for the file's owning object.
// Issue order/duplicates and coordinates are preserved; no CLI dump is parsed.
func (c *Checker) Check(filename string) []Issue {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 c.require()
 file := c.registry.@getFileByName@(str(filename))
 if file == nil { panic("file is not in the registry: " + filename) }
 obj := c.registry.@findObjectForFile@(file)
 if obj == nil { panic("object is not in the registry: " + filename) }
 return c.checkObject(obj)
}

// CheckObject uses the registry lookup verbatim: names are case insensitive,
// object types are case sensitive. A missing object returns nil, false.
func (c *Checker) CheckObject(typ, name string) ([]Issue, bool) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 c.require()
 obj := c.registry.@getObject@(present(str(typ)), present(str(name)))
 if obj == nil { return nil, false }
 return c.checkObject(obj), true
}

func (c *Checker) countParse() {
 dirty := int32(0)
 for object := range c.pending { if object.@isDirty@() { dirty++ } }
 if dirty > 0 { c.stats.ParseRuns++; c.stats.ParseObjects += dirty }
}

func (c *Checker) checkObject(obj @Object@) []Issue {
 c.countParse()
 issues := c.registry.@findIssuesObject@(obj)
 clear(c.pending)
 out := make([]Issue, 0, libraryLength(issues))
 for at := int32(0); at < libraryLength(issues); at++ {
  issue := any(libraryAt(issues, at)).(@Issue@)
  start, end := issue.@getStart@(), issue.@getEnd@()
  out = append(out, Issue{Filename: issue.@getFilename@().String(), Key: issue.@getKey@().String(), Severity: issue.@getSeverity@().String(), Message: issue.@getMessage@().String(),
   Row: libraryCoordinate(start.@getRow@()), Column: libraryCoordinate(start.@getCol@()), EndRow: libraryCoordinate(end.@getRow@()), EndColumn: libraryCoordinate(end.@getCol@())})
 }
 return out
}
func (c *Checker) Stats() Stats { libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock(); return c.stats }

// Pos retains raw, one-based abaplint coordinates. End positions are exclusive.
type Pos struct { Row, Col int32 }
// Pragma records lexer identity, which concatTokens needs even if a caller
// changes Str. String length for adjacency is measured in UTF-16 code units.
type Token struct { Str string; Start, End Pos; Pragma bool }
type Node struct {
 Kind string
 Statement bool
 Start, End Pos
 Tokens []Token
 Children []Node
 // The pinned core follows only the first-child chain. For every structure
 // with valid token bounds this is its first depth-first statement, so nil.
 FirstStatement *Node
}
type FileTree struct { Filename string; Structure *Node; Statements []Node }

// ConcatTokens matches StatementNode.concatTokens, skipping pragma tokens
// without changing the previous non-pragma token used for adjacency.
func ConcatTokens(tokens []Token) string {
 var out strings.Builder
 var prev *Token
 for i := range tokens {
  token := &tokens[i]
  if token.Pragma { continue }
  if out.Len() != 0 && (prev == nil || prev.Start.Row != token.Start.Row || int64(prev.Start.Col) + int64(len(utf16.Encode([]rune(prev.Str)))) != int64(token.Start.Col)) { out.WriteByte(' ') }
  out.WriteString(token.Str)
  prev = token
 }
 return out.String()
}

func libraryPos(pos @Position@) Pos {
 return Pos{Row: libraryCoordinate(pos.@getRow@()), Col: libraryCoordinate(pos.@getCol@())}
}
func libraryToken(token @AbstractToken@) Token {
 return Token{Str: token.@getStr@().String(), Start: libraryPos(token.@getStart@()), End: libraryPos(token.@getEnd@()), Pragma: descriptorInstance(token, &@PragmaDescriptor@)}
}
func libraryStatement(statement @StatementNode@) Node {
 out := Node{Kind: classOf(statement.@get@()).Name.String(), Statement: true,
  Start: libraryPos(statement.@getFirstToken@().@getStart@()), End: libraryPos(statement.@getLastToken@().@getEnd@())}
 tokens := statement.@getTokens@()
 out.Tokens = make([]Token, 0, libraryLength(tokens))
 for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(tokens); i++ { out.Tokens = append(out.Tokens, libraryToken(libraryUnwrap(libraryAt(tokens, i)).(@AbstractToken@))) }
 return out
}
func libraryStructure(structure @StructureNode@) Node {
 out := Node{Kind: classOf(structure.@get@()).Name.String()}
 children := structure.@getChildren@()
 if libraryLength(children) > 0 {
  out.Start = libraryPos(structure.@getFirstToken@().@getStart@())
  out.End = libraryPos(structure.@getLastToken@().@getEnd@())
 }
 out.Children = make([]Node, 0, libraryLength(children))
 for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(children); i++ {
  child := libraryUnwrap(libraryAt(children, i))
  switch node := child.(type) {
  case @StatementNode@: out.Children = append(out.Children, libraryStatement(node))
  case @StructureNode@: out.Children = append(out.Children, libraryStructure(node))
  default: panic(fmt.Sprintf("unexpected structure child %T", child))
  }
 }
 return out
}
func libraryUnwrap(value any) any {
 if d, ok := value.(*dynamic); ok { if d == nil { return nil }; return d.Value }
 return value
}

// Tree parses pending edits, then copies outline data while holding libraryMu.
// Non-ABAP objects are found but have no ABAP files (an empty slice).
func (c *Checker) Tree(typ, name string) ([]FileTree, bool) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 c.require()
 obj := c.registry.@getObject@(present(str(typ)), present(str(name)))
 if obj == nil { return nil, false }
 c.countParse()
 c.registry.@parse@()
 clear(c.pending)
 return libraryTree(obj), true
}

// TreeOf builds an isolated outline from the supplied files using the core's
// default configuration. INCLUDEs and macros in objects outside files are absent.
// Use TreeOfWithConfig to match a Checker's release and global macro settings.
func TreeOf(files []File, typ, name string) ([]FileTree, bool) {
 return TreeOfWithConfig(files, typ, name, "{}")
}

// TreeOfWithConfig is TreeOf with the same configuration accepted by Prime.
// No baseline or reader index is built. Core access and snapshot copying remain
// serialised with all Checkers, and returned slices never alias the registry.
func TreeOfWithConfig(files []File, typ, name, config string) ([]FileTree, bool) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 registry := @newRegistry@(@newConfig@(str(config)))
 for _, file := range files { registry.@addFile@(@newFile@(str(file.Filename), str(file.Raw))) }
 @clearParsingPerformance@()
 // The outline needs parsing and cross-include macros, but not global OO/DDIC
 // type discovery. Use the pinned registry's own per-object parser/configuration.
 objects := registry.@getObjects@()
 defer objects.@close@()
 for {
  next := objects.@next@()
  if next.@done@ { break }
  registry.@parsePrivate@(next.@value@)
 }
 @newCrossIncludeMacros@(registry).@run@()
 obj := registry.@getObject@(present(str(typ)), present(str(name)))
 if obj == nil { return nil, false }
 return libraryTree(obj), true
}

// Caller holds libraryMu and has parsed the owning registry.
func libraryTree(obj @Object@) []FileTree {
 out := make([]FileTree, 0)
 abap, ok := obj.(@ABAPObject@)
 if !ok { return out }
 files := abap.@getABAPFiles@()
 ordered := make([]@ABAPFile@, 0, libraryLength(files))
 if obj.@getType@().String() == "CLAS" || obj.@getType@().String() == "INTF" {
  files = abap.@getSequencedFiles@()
  for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(files); i++ { ordered = append(ordered, libraryUnwrap(libraryAt(files, i)).(@ABAPFile@)) }
 } else {
  main := abap.@getMainABAPFile@()
  if main != nil { ordered = append(ordered, main) }
  for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(files); i++ { file := libraryUnwrap(libraryAt(files, i)).(@ABAPFile@); if file != main { ordered = append(ordered, file) } }
 }
 for _, file := range ordered {
  tree := FileTree{Filename: file.@getFilename@().String()}
  if structure := file.@getStructure@(); structure != nil { node := libraryStructure(structure); tree.Structure = &node }
  statements := file.@getStatements@()
  tree.Statements = make([]Node, 0, libraryLength(statements))
  for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(statements); i++ { tree.Statements = append(tree.Statements, libraryStatement(libraryUnwrap(libraryAt(statements, i)).(@StatementNode@))) }
  out = append(out, tree)
 }
 return out
}

// Expression copies CDS expression nodes, omitting TokenNode children. Bounds
// retain raw one-based token positions, including the last token's getEnd().
type Expression struct { Kind, Text string; Start, End Pos; Children []Expression }

func libraryExpression(node @ExpressionNode@) Expression {
 out := Expression{Kind: classOf(node.@get@()).Name.String(), Text: node.@concatTokens@().String(),
  Start: libraryPos(node.@getFirstToken@().@getStart@()), End: libraryPos(node.@getLastToken@().@getEnd@())}
 children := node.@getChildren@()
 for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(children); i++ {
  if child, ok := libraryUnwrap(libraryAt(children, i)).(@ExpressionNode@); ok { out.Children = append(out.Children, libraryExpression(child)) }
 }
 return out
}

// CDS parses pending edits before looking up a DDLS object. An absent tree or
// SQL view name remains nil; a defined empty SQL view name remains &"".
func (c *Checker) CDS(name string) (tree *Expression, sqlView *string, found bool) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 c.require()
 c.countParse()
 c.registry.@parse@()
 clear(c.pending)
 obj := c.registry.@getObject@(present(str("DDLS")), present(str(name)))
 if obj == nil { return nil, nil, false }
 definition := obj.(@DataDefinition@)
 if node := definition.@getTree@(); node != nil { out := libraryExpression(node); tree = &out }
 if sql := definition.@getSQLViewName@(); sql.Has { out := sql.Value.String(); sqlView = &out }
 return tree, sqlView, true
}

// DDIC copies TABL/VIEW components only for StructureType results. A different
// type yields nil components; an empty StructureType yields a non-nil empty slice.
// Component and key order/case are exactly those returned by the core.
func (c *Checker) DDIC(typ, name string) (components, keys []string, found bool) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 c.require()
 c.countParse()
 c.registry.@parse@()
 clear(c.pending)
 obj := c.registry.@getObject@(present(str(typ)), present(str(name)))
 if obj == nil { return nil, nil, false }
 var parsed @AbstractType@
 var coreKeys *array[jsString]
 switch object := obj.(type) {
 case @Table@:
  parsed = object.@parseType@(c.registry, optional[jsString]{}, optional[jsString]{})
  coreKeys = object.@listKeys@(c.registry)
 case @View@:
  parsed = object.@parseType@(c.registry, optional[jsString]{}, optional[jsString]{})
  coreKeys = object.@listKeys@()
 }
 if structure, ok := parsed.(@StructureType@); ok {
  values := structure.@getComponents@()
  components = make([]string, 0, libraryLength(values))
  for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(values); i++ {
   component := libraryUnwrap(libraryAt(values, i)).(@Component@)
   components = append(components, component.@name@.String())
  }
 }
 if coreKeys != nil {
  for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(coreKeys); i++ { keys = append(keys, libraryAt(coreKeys, i).String()) }
 }
 return components, keys, true
}

// Files parses pending edits before lookup and copies files in object order,
// preserving logical filenames and exact raw source bytes.
func (c *Checker) Files(typ, name string) (files []File, found bool) {
 libraryMu.Lock(); defer libraryMu.Unlock()
 c.require()
 c.countParse()
 c.registry.@parse@()
 clear(c.pending)
 obj := c.registry.@getObject@(present(str(typ)), present(str(name)))
 if obj == nil { return nil, false }
 values := obj.@getFiles@()
 for i := int32(0); i < libraryLength(values); i++ {
  file := libraryUnwrap(libraryAt(values, i)).(@File@)
  files = append(files, File{Filename: file.@getFilename@().String(), Raw: file.@getRaw@().String()})
 }
 return files, true
}
